newsitem.title: USA: Missouri Gov. signs budget and seeks court opinion.
newsitem.headline: Missouri Gov. signs budget and seeks court opinion.

text.p: Missouri Gov. Mel Carnahan signed a $14.7 billion all-funds budget for fiscal 1998 Thursday that includes a controversial measure denying payments to Planned Parenthood, a spokesman said.

Carnahan at the same time said he has asked the state attorney general to seek a court ruling to determine whether a ruling last year overturning a similar funding ban on Planned Parenthood would apply to the current legislation, Chris Sifford said.

"The governor feels that this is the quickest way to move forward with our family planning program," Sifford said. "Otherwise, we would have to wait until after a veto session before it could be settled in the courts.
"This way, hopefully we can get a ruling within days," Sifford said.
Lawmakers in May broke a budget stalemate by adopting a compromise health package eliminating Planned Parenthood funding from the budget.
Carnahan opposed the action, which he said appeared to directly violate a federal court ruling that barred Missouri from excluding any provider of family services from the budget.
The budget includes $552.5 million for capital improvements over the next two years.
The budget also provides $146.4 million for two new 1,500-bed men's prisons and $6.1 million for an additional 256 beds for a women's housing unit at a prison now under construction.
